progression.prerequisiteKnowledge: dynamic equilibrium means equal non-zero rates in a closed system (C1); the faster rate falls and the slower rate rises until they meet (C2); adding or removing a substance changes one rate first (C3); only collisions with at least the activation energy react, and a catalyst lowers it for both directions (C3, C4b); squeeze favours fewer gas particles and argon at fixed volume changes nothing (C4a); K expression leaves out solids (C5); Q compared with K gives the direction, "Q chases K" (C8). Nothing is re-derived; each is recalled in one clause.
progression.startsWith: Here's an answer that sounds right but on its own explains nothing: Le Chatelier's principle says it shifts right. By the end you'll know what to write instead. We'll work through three types of equilibrium question in full: explain with collision theory, graphs after a change, and the no-shift traps. Then you try two. Temperature, industry and open systems come in part two.
progression.stopsAfter: recognising three question types from their wording; writing the five-step collision-theory answer and finishing on the named species; describing a concentration-time and an amount-time graph after the same disturbance, reading the axis label first; deciding that argon at fixed volume, a catalyst or an added pure solid does not shift the mixture and saying why with Q. No industrial or open-system questions (proposed part 3), no K calculations, no ICE, no temperature and K, no Ksp or Ka.
progression.nextLesson: part 2 of this practice series (chem-m5-g03: calculation types: writing K, ICE tables, Q against K, finding the amount added; confirm it also covers the quadratic behind the settled values in q2, and add the equal-gas-count Q case if root accepts the proposal above). Then chem-m5-c09 (temperature and K), and the proposed part 3 after it. If the playlist runs part 2 first, change the chip in the decision board.

teaching.task: An equilibrium question gives you a change and asks you to explain or predict. How do you spot the type, what do you write, and which slips ruin the answer?
teaching.causalExplanation: The collision-theory answer is built from the C3 mechanism (one rate changes first, the other is unchanged at that instant, the faster rate falls and the slower rises) in q1 and again in try1. The graph lines come from the squeeze (all concentrations double because concentration is amount over volume) separate from the reaction (curves), and the amount graph has no jump because nothing is added or removed. The no-shift test is "does Q still equal K?", linked to C8, with the argon collision question answered (the reacting gases are no more crowded).
teaching.conversationalApproach: Here's an answer that sounds right but on its own explains nothing: Le Chatelier's principle says it shifts right. Type one, the one that catches the most people: explain with collision theory. Build the answer in the order things happen. Three classic slips. Type two: graphs after a disturbance. Start with the squeeze. Now the response. Now the amount in moles. So read the axis label first. Type three: the no-shift traps. The method is one question: does Q still equal K? Argon bumps into things, but the forward reaction needs two N O two molecules to meet and the reverse needs N two O four to split, and the reacting gases are no more crowded. Two slips: pressure rises, so it shifts to fewer particles, and pressure rises, so the temperature rises. Your turn. Then, in your own time, write the full five lines and check them against this. One more, a graph. The volume changed, and it was decreased. Find the words that give the type away.
teaching.openingDecision: Here's an answer that sounds right but on its own explains nothing: Le Chatelier's principle says it shifts right. By the end you'll know what to write instead. We'll work through three types of equilibrium question in full: explain with collision theory, graphs after a change, and the no-shift traps. Then you try two. Temperature, industry and open systems come in part two.
teaching.understandingCheck: two unseen 10 s attempts with every condition visible, both bounded decisions; the type board dims during both. The key notes hold is a separate quiet hold of about 60 s.

design.visualSystem: One practice board throughout. Top-left the question card (the full worded question, as an exam prints it, with the tag "HSC-style question, written for HSCScience"); during each walkthrough the card shrinks to a strip and each given is underlined in amber in the question text at its cue (no givens card). The right two thirds hold the diagram or graph; the lower left holds the answer as it builds. A thin question-type board runs along the top with the current type lit; it ticks a type off when its segment ends, and it dims to an outline during both countdowns, because it names the method. Colour key: forward blue, reverse amber, equal teal; NO2 brown, N2O4 pale grey; argon pale blue dots; amber only for underlined givens; mistakes in a muted red cross-out with the correction in green ink beside it. Clutter rule: besides the question strip and the type board, at most about three bright text items in the working area at once; finished answer lines dim while the next writes; each tag fades when the next cue lands.

"the forward reaction increases" crossed, green "the forward rate . earlier working clears. on "Start with the squeeze" amber underlines land on "0. on "Two gas particles become one" the syringe particle view shows two NO2 dots joining into one N2O4 pair (looped once). the second axes fill beside the first (the concentration graph shrinks to half size, labelled "concentration"; the amount graph is labelled "amount (mol)", same time axis, vertical lines at t1 aligned). on "axis label" both axis titles take an amber ring (tag "read this first"). earlier working clears. the vessel gains argon dots on "Argon" (pale blue, ten dots drop in), the gauge rises from 1 to 2. two slips write on and are crossed out, with green corrections: "shifts to fewer particles" with "pressure alone is not a disturbance here"; "pressure up so temperature up" with "no net reaction, no net heat change". fresh board. the card shrinks to a strip; amber underlines land on "rigid", "Extra nitrogen", "temperature does not change" and "concentration of hydrogen" in the opening sentences. fresh board. amber underline on "temperature is kept constant throughout". the type board returns full size as a two-column table, "You see" on the left and "You do" on the right, one row per cue: "using collision theory, explain" | "the five-line chain (change, collisions, rate, other rate, net, named species, level)" (with the five-line chain as a small icon strip); "sketch or describe the graph" | "axis label first: one line jumps (added or removed); every gas jumps (volume); amounts never jump on a squeeze"; "argon at fixed volume, catalyst, added solid" | "does Q still equal K? If yes, no shift". Heading on screen: "Key notes: what to write in your book".

scenes.visualReference: the vessel stays on the right with the C3 rate bars beside it (forward blue, reverse amber, equal teal bracket at the start). On line 5 the bars move together to the teal "equal" bracket. A tag, "rate: how fast; reaction: the whole change", appears at line 2 and stays. The chain aid does not appear yet. Hold about 2 seconds.
